audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 11, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness, reception-history, and political audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for foreign-wife blame, plural marriage and concubinage, interfaith worship, gendered responsibility, Edomite massacre, child refugee Hadad, Egyptian asylum, adversary theology, forced labor, prophetic succession, attempted political killing, and imperial collapse.

verses.restored: King Solomon loved many foreign women, besides Pharaoh's daughter: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women.

familiar.text: But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites;

modern.text: King Solomon, however, loved many foreign women along with the daughter of Pharaoh—women of Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon, as well as Hittite women.

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אָהַ֞ב נָשִׁ֧ים נָכְרִיּ֛וֹת רַבּ֖וֹת וְאֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹ֑ה מוֹאֲבִיּ֤וֹת עַמֳּנִיּוֹת֙ אֲדֹ֣מִיֹּ֔ת צֵדְנִיֹּ֖ת חִתִּיֹּֽת

verses.restored: From nations of which YHWH said to children of Israel, You shall not enter among them and they shall not enter among you, for surely they will turn your heart after their gods. Solomon clung to them in love.

familiar.text: Of the nations concerning which the LORD said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.

modern.text: These women were from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, “You must not intermarry with them, for surely they will turn your hearts after their gods.” Yet Solomon clung to these women in love.

original.text: מִן הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר יְהוָה֩ אֶל בְּנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֹֽא תָבֹ֣אוּ בָהֶ֗ם וְהֵם֙ לֹא יָבֹ֣אוּ בָכֶ֔ם אָכֵן֙ יַטּ֣וּ אֶת לְבַבְכֶ֔ם אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם בָּהֶ֛ם דָּבַ֥ק שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְאַהֲבָֽה

verses.restored: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; his wives turned his heart.

familiar.text: And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.

modern.text: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines—and his wives turned his heart away.

original.text: וַיְהִי ל֣וֹ נָשִׁ֗ים שָׂרוֹת֙ שְׁבַ֣ע מֵא֔וֹת וּפִֽלַגְשִׁ֖ים שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת וַיַּטּ֥וּ נָשָׁ֖יו אֶת לִבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not whole with YHWH his Divine as heart of David his father.

familiar.text: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.

modern.text: For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and he was not wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David had been.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י לְעֵת֙ זִקְנַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה נָשָׁיו֙ הִטּ֣וּ אֶת לְבָב֔וֹ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְלֹא הָיָ֨ה לְבָב֤וֹ שָׁלֵם֙ עִם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו כִּלְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֥יד אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Solomon walked after Ashtoreth goddess of Sidonians and after Milcom detestable thing/god of Ammonites.

familiar.text: For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

modern.text: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֣י עַשְׁתֹּ֔רֶת אֱלֹהֵ֖י צִדֹנִ֑ים וְאַחֲרֵ֣י מִלְכֹּ֔ם שִׁקֻּ֖ץ עַמֹּנִֽים

verses.restored: Solomon did evil in eyes of YHWH and did not fully follow YHWH as David his father.

familiar.text: And Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD, and went not fully after the LORD, as did David his father.

modern.text: So Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD; unlike his father David, he did not follow the LORD completely.

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א מִלֵּ֛א אַחֲרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, detestable thing/god of Moab, on hill before Jerusalem, and for Molech, detestable thing/god of children of Ammon.

familiar.text: Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.

modern.text: At that time on a hill east of Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.

original.text: אָז֩ יִבְנֶ֨ה שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בָּמָ֗ה לִכְמוֹשׁ֙ שִׁקֻּ֣ץ מוֹאָ֔ב בָּהָ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל פְּנֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וּלְמֹ֕לֶךְ שִׁקֻּ֖ץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: Thus he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.

familiar.text: And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

modern.text: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods. God’s Anger against Solomon

original.text: וְכֵ֣ן עָשָׂ֔ה לְכָל נָשָׁ֖יו הַנָּכְרִיּ֑וֹת מַקְטִיר֥וֹת וּֽמְזַבְּח֖וֹת לֵאלֹהֵיהֶֽן

verses.restored: YHWH became angry with Solomon because his heart turned from YHWH, Divine of Israel, who appeared to him twice,

familiar.text: And the LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the LORD God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice,

modern.text: Now the LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.

original.text: וַיִּתְאַנַּ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בִּשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה כִּֽי נָטָ֣ה לְבָב֗וֹ מֵעִ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַנִּרְאָ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם

verses.restored: and commanded him concerning this matter not to walk after other gods; but he did not keep what YHWH commanded.

familiar.text: And had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the LORD commanded.

modern.text: Although He had warned Solomon explicitly not to follow other gods, Solomon did not keep the LORD’s command.

original.text: וְצִוָּ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ עַל הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְבִ֨לְתִּי לֶ֔כֶת אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔ר אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖ה יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: YHWH said to Solomon, Because this is with you and you did not keep my covenant and statutes I commanded, tearing I will tear kingdom from you and give it to your servant.

familiar.text: Wherefore the LORD said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you have done this and have not kept My covenant and My statutes, which I have commanded you, I will tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽיְתָה זֹּ֣את עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֨רְתָּ֙ בְּרִיתִ֣י וְחֻקֹּתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי עָלֶ֑יךָ קָרֹ֨עַ אֶקְרַ֤ע אֶת הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֖יהָ לְעַבְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: Yet in your days I will not do it, for sake of David your father; from hand of your son I will tear it.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.

modern.text: Nevertheless, for the sake of your father David, I will not do it during your lifetime; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.

original.text: אַךְ בְּיָמֶ֨יךָ֙ לֹ֣א אֶעֱשֶׂ֔נָּה לְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יךָ מִיַּ֥ד בִּנְךָ֖ אֶקְרָעֶֽנָּה

verses.restored: Only I will not tear away all kingdom; one tribe I will give to your son for sake of David my servant and Jerusalem which I chose.

familiar.text: Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.

modern.text: Yet I will not tear the whole kingdom away from him. I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.” Hadad’s Return

original.text: רַ֤ק אֶת כָּל הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ לֹ֣א אֶקְרָ֔ע שֵׁ֥בֶט אֶחָ֖ד אֶתֵּ֣ן לִבְנֶ֑ךָ לְמַ֨עַן֙ דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י וּלְמַ֥עַן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּחָֽרְתִּי

verses.restored: YHWH raised an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, from royal seed in Edom.

familiar.text: And the LORD stirred up an adversary unto Solomon, Hadad the Edomite: he was of the king’s seed in Edom.

modern.text: Then the LORD raised up against Solomon an adversary, Hadad the Edomite, from the royal line of Edom.

original.text: וַיָּ֨קֶם יְהוָ֤ה שָׂטָן֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֖ת הֲדַ֣ד הָאֲדֹמִ֑י מִזֶּ֧רַע הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ ה֖וּא בֶּאֱדֽוֹם

verses.restored: When David was in Edom and Joab commander of army went up to bury slain, after striking every male in Edom—

familiar.text: For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host was gone up to bury the slain, after he had smitten every male in Edom;

modern.text: Earlier, when David was in Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּֽהְי֤וֹת דָּוִד֙ אֶת אֱד֔וֹם בַּעֲל֗וֹת יוֹאָב֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א לְקַבֵּ֖ר אֶת הַחֲלָלִ֑ים וַיַּ֥ךְ כָּל זָכָ֖ר בֶּאֱדֽוֹם

verses.restored: for six months Joab remained there with all Israel until he cut off every male in Edom—

familiar.text: (For six months did Joab remain there with all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom:)

modern.text: Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.

original.text: כִּ֣י שֵׁ֧שֶׁת חֳדָשִׁ֛ים יָֽשַׁב שָׁ֥ם יוֹאָ֖ב וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַד הִכְרִ֥ית כָּל זָכָ֖ר בֶּאֱדֽוֹם

verses.restored: Hadad fled, he and Edomite men from servants of his father with him, to go to Egypt; Hadad was a small child.

familiar.text: That Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants with him, to go into Egypt; Hadad being yet a little child.

modern.text: But Hadad, still just a young boy, had fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites who were servants of his father.

original.text: וַיִּבְרַ֣ח אֲדַ֡ד הוּא֩ וַאֲנָשִׁ֨ים אֲדֹמִיִּ֜ים מֵעַבְדֵ֥י אָבִ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ לָב֣וֹא מִצְרָ֑יִם וַהֲדַ֖ד נַ֥עַר קָטָֽן

verses.restored: They arose from Midian, came to Paran, took men from Paran with them, and came to Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt. Pharaoh gave him a house, appointed food for him, and gave him land.

familiar.text: And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran: and they took men with them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, unto Pharaoh king of Egypt; which gave him an house, and appointed him victuals, and gave him land.

modern.text: Hadad and his men set out from Midian and went to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and went to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house and land and provided him with food.

original.text: וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ֙ מִמִּדְיָ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ פָּארָ֑ן וַיִּקְחוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים עִמָּ֜ם מִפָּארָ֗ן וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּתֶּן ל֣וֹ בַ֗יִת וְלֶ֨חֶם֙ אָ֣מַר ל֔וֹ וְאֶ֖רֶץ נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ

verses.restored: Hadad found great favor in eyes of Pharaoh, who gave him as wife sister of his own wife, sister of Tahpenes the queen.

familiar.text: And Hadad found great favour in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.

modern.text: There Hadad found such great favor in the sight of Pharaoh that he gave to him in marriage the sister of Queen Tahpenes, his own wife.

original.text: וַיִּמְצָא֙ הֲדַ֥ד חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּתֶּן ל֤וֹ אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת אֲח֣וֹת אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ אֲח֖וֹת תַּחְפְּנֵ֥יס הַגְּבִירָֽה

verses.restored: Sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house; Genubath was in Pharaoh's household among Pharaoh's sons.

familiar.text: And the sister of Tahpenes bare him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house: and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s household among the sons of Pharaoh.

modern.text: And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad a son named Genubath. Tahpenes herself weaned him in Pharaoh’s palace, and Genubath lived there among the sons of Pharaoh.

original.text: וַתֵּ֨לֶד ל֜וֹ אֲח֣וֹת תַּחְפְּנֵ֗יס אֵ֚ת גְּנֻבַ֣ת בְּנ֔וֹ וַתִּגְמְלֵ֣הוּ תַחְפְּנֵ֔ס בְּת֖וֹךְ בֵּ֣ית פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י גְנֻבַת֙ בֵּ֣ית פַּרְעֹ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה

verses.restored: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David lay with his ancestors and Joab commander of army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Send me away, that I may go to my land.

familiar.text: And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to mine own country.

modern.text: When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had rested with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, was dead, he said to Pharaoh, “Let me go, that I may return to my own country.”

original.text: וַהֲדַ֞ד שָׁמַ֣ע בְּמִצְרַ֗יִם כִּֽי שָׁכַ֤ב דָּוִד֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וְכִי מֵ֖ת יוֹאָ֣ב שַֽׂר הַצָּבָ֑א וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הֲדַד֙ אֶל פַּרְעֹ֔ה שַׁלְּחֵ֖נִי וְאֵלֵ֥ךְ אֶל אַרְצִֽי

verses.restored: Pharaoh said, What have you lacked with me that you seek to go to your land? He said, Nothing, but sending, send me away.

familiar.text: Then Pharaoh said unto him, But what hast thou lacked with me, that, behold, thou seekest to go to thine own country? And he answered, Nothing: howbeit let me go in any wise.

modern.text: But Pharaoh asked him, “What have you lacked here with me that you suddenly want to go back to your own country?” “Nothing,” Hadad replied, “but please let me go.” Rezon’s Hostility

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ פַרְעֹ֗ה כִּ֠י מָה אַתָּ֤ה חָסֵר֙ עִמִּ֔י וְהִנְּךָ֥ מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לָלֶ֣כֶת אֶל אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לֹ֔א כִּ֥י שַׁלֵּ֖חַ תְּשַׁלְּחֵֽנִי

verses.restored: Divine raised another adversary against Solomon: Rezon son of Eliada, who fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah.

familiar.text: And God stirred him up another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliadah, which fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah:

modern.text: And God raised up against Solomon another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah,

original.text: וַיָּ֨קֶם אֱלֹהִ֥ים לוֹ֙ שָׂטָ֔ן אֶת רְז֖וֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָדָ֑ע אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֗ח מֵאֵ֛ת הֲדַדְעֶ֥זֶר מֶֽלֶךְ צוֹבָ֖ה אֲדֹנָֽיו

verses.restored: He gathered men to himself and became commander of a band when David killed those of Zobah. They went to Damascus, lived there, and reigned in Damascus.

familiar.text: And he gathered men unto him, and became captain over a band, when David slew them of Zobah: and they went to Damascus, and dwelt therein, and reigned in Damascus.

modern.text: and had gathered men to himself. When David killed the Zobaites, Rezon captained a band of raiders and went to Damascus, where they settled and gained control.

original.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ עָלָיו֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיְהִ֣י שַׂר גְּד֔וּד בַּהֲרֹ֥ג דָּוִ֖ד אֹתָ֑ם וַיֵּלְכ֤וּ דַמֶּ֨שֶׂק֙ וַיֵּ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ וַֽיִּמְלְכ֖וּ בְּדַמָּֽשֶׂק

verses.restored: He was an adversary to Israel all days of Solomon, besides evil Hadad did. He loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.

familiar.text: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, beside the mischief that Hadad did: and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.

modern.text: Rezon was Israel’s enemy throughout the days of Solomon, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. So Rezon ruled over Aram with hostility toward Israel. Jeroboam’s Rebellion

translation_notes: The chapter blames foreign wives for turning Solomon's heart, but Solomon is the king who accumulated one thousand women within a system of dynastic marriage, concubinage, and likely coercion. Responsibility belongs to him, not to women's ethnicity.

Foreign women and their religions must not be portrayed as inherently corrupting. Interfaith contact is not the same as imperial accumulation, coercive marriage, or abandoning covenantal responsibility.
The labels 'detestable thing' reflect polemical religious language. They may not justify persecution, vandalism, forced conversion, antisemitism, Islamophobia, or contempt toward living traditions.
Hadad's story reveals the imperial violence hidden beneath Solomon's peace: David and Joab killed every male in Edom over six months, and a small child fled into Egyptian asylum.
Hadad's desire to return home is not irrational ingratitude toward Egypt; refugees may value safety and still long for homeland.
Rezon's movement also emerges from Davidic war. Political adversaries are survivors and agents, not merely instruments raised to punish Solomon.
Jeroboam is first a supervisor inside Solomon's forced-labor system. The coming rupture is tied to exploitation as well as prophetic symbolism.
The narrative praises David's obedience in sweeping terms despite the books' own record. Royal idealization must be held beside Bathsheba, Uriah, census plague, Edom, and other harms.
Solomon attempts to kill a political rival, driving Jeroboam into the same Egyptian asylum that sheltered Hadad.
safety_note: Do not blame women, foreigners, interfaith relationships, aging, or minority religions for Solomon's collapse. Center royal accumulation, coercive marriage, forced labor, imperial massacre, refugee survival, and attempted political assassination.
